title: Wolf and Garden
premise: Quentin Eastwick tends the Hollow Gate, a sealed door between the human city of Vell and the wild realm of Thorn, selling harmless charms to survive in a city that burns mages. When a bookbinder named Isolde Vane discovers her own name and tonight's date in a century-old prophecy, she is drawn through the gate and bound to the covenant that once kept both realms alive. As the moon wanes toward its thirteenth turn, Quentin and Isolde must gather the scattered oaths of three dead wardens, outwit the Gate's original architect who feeds on broken promises, and choose between sealing the realms forever or reforging the covenant at the cost of Quentin's inherited duty — and his life. In the end, Isolde rewrites the prophecy's final line with her own blood, sparing Quentin but binding herself as the new keeper, and the two lovers share a gate instead of a home.
about_author: Jonah Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forbidden grimoires before turning to fiction. They live near a very old forest and insist, politely, that the wolves started it.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He sells luck-knots and fever-charms in Vell's night market while hiding his true work: keeping the Hollow Gate shut beneath his shop. A raid by the Ministry of Unnatural Affairs nearly exposes him. Emotional beat: weary vigilance, the loneliness of a secret kept for three years.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ink
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Restoring a water-damaged prophecy book, Isolde finds her own name beside tomorrow's date and a sketch of a man she's never met. That evening she walks into Quentin's stall exactly as foretold. Emotional beat: uncanny dread braided with irresistible curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Moon Counts
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The prophecy describes thirteen moon-turns ending in a choice: seal or sever. Quentin tries to send Isolde away; she refuses. The first moon-turn mark appears on her wrist. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership forged under threat.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Shop
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He shows Isolde the Hollow Gate — a door of woven thorn and iron that hums when she touches it. The gate recognizes her bloodline; she is descended from the covenant's first witness. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear of what inheritance demands.

chapters.title: Ministry of Ash
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The Ministry arrests Quentin's fence, Wren, for trafficking charms. Interrogation reveals the Ministry knows about the gate and wants it opened, not destroyed. Emotional beat: the dawning realization that the law itself is a predator.

chapters.title: The First Oath: Riverkeeper
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Following the prophecy, they seek the drowned shrine of the Riverkeeper, first of three dead wardens whose oaths must be reforged. Quentin nearly drowns holding the door open for Isolde. Emotional beat: first proof they will bleed for each other.

chapters.title: Thornlight
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. On the far side of the shrine they glimpse Thorn: a realm of luminous briars and exiled magic. A fox-spirit warns that the Architect still walks and eats promises. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold His Name
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Flashback chapters within the present: how Quentin inherited keeper-ship from his dying mother, who traded her name to the Architect to buy him three safe years. The debt comes due on the thirteenth turn. Emotional beat: guilt and the weight of inherited bargains.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde breaks Wren out of the Ministry cells using a charm Quentin forbade — one that costs a memory. She forgets her sister's face. Emotional beat: the price of survival made intimate and irreversible.

chapters.title: The Second Oath: Stonefather
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In the quarries below Vell, the Stonefather's oath sleeps inside a petrified giant. The Ministry ambushes them; Quentin reveals his magic openly to save Isolde, making them both fugitives. Emotional beat: love declared through sacrifice, safety abandoned.

chapters.title: Fugitives' Moon
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Hiding in Thorn's borderlands, the two share quiet days gathering herbs and repairing charms — a stolen domesticity neither expected. The seventh moon-turn mark appears. Emotional beat: tenderness blooming in hostile ground.

chapters.title: The Architect's Invitation
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The Architect appears wearing Quentin's mother's face, offering to release Quentin's debt if Isolde delivers the two gathered oaths. She pretends to consider. Emotional beat: cold terror masked as diplomacy.

chapters.title: Prophecy Against Prophecy
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Isolde restores the prophecy book fully and finds a second, hidden text: the first witness's testimony, revealing the covenant was never meant to be sealed — only renewed by a willing heir. Emotional beat: hope that reframes everything.

chapters.title: The Third Oath: Skywarden
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The third oath lies at the top of the Spire of Bells, guarded by the Ministry's new weapon: a hollowed mage. Quentin recognizes his old teacher. To take the oath he must unmake what remains of him. Emotional beat: grief as the cost of duty.

chapters.title: Turn Twelve
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. With all three oaths gathered, the marks on Isolde's wrist burn. The Architect strikes, stealing the oaths and Wren, and reveals the final line of the prophecy names a death — Quentin's. Emotional beat: despair at the edge of the last turn.

chapters.title: The Empty Shop
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin prepares to die quietly, writing letters and dismantling his wards so Isolde can't trade herself for him. She reads every letter and refuses every arrangement. Emotional beat: love against self-sacrifice, argued in ink.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the Hollow Gate under the full moon, the Architect forces the door wide. Thorn bleeds into Vell; the city's outlawed magic rises like floodwater. Quentin offers his life; Isolde offers something the Architect cannot digest — a promise freely rewritten. Emotional beat: climax, defiance at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Rewritten Line
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Using the first witness's method, Isolde writes a new covenant in her own blood: not seal, not sever, but shared keeping. The Architect, starved of a broken promise, unravels. Quentin survives, freed of his mother's debt. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with permanence.

chapters.title: Keeper and Witness
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Ministry, half-destroyed and half-convinced, negotiates a truce: magic returns to Vell under the new covenant. Quentin keeps the gate; Isolde keeps the book. Emotional beat: exhausted peace, the strange gentleness after war.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Wren, freed, carries a fragment of Isolde's lost memory — her sister's face — recovered from the Architect's leavings. Isolde chooses not to reclaim it, honoring what it bought. Emotional beat: acceptance of irrevocable cost.

chapters.title: Two Sides of One Door
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Spring in Vell; briar-light in Thorn. Quentin and Isolde build their lives on either side of the gate, meeting at its threshold each dusk. The prophecy book now writes blank pages, waiting. Emotional beat: love redefined as a shared doorway rather than a shared roof.

chapters.title: The Garden Grows Back
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV, epilogue. A year later, a child arrives at the shop carrying a book with her own name in it — the covenant choosing its next witness early. Isolde and Quentin exchange a look over the counter: the story continues. Emotional beat: inheritance as gift, not burden; an open, hopeful ending.
